chunks: Very soon you will be overwhelmed with the gloom of its shades, the severity of its illness, the darkness of its distresses, the nonsense utterances of its pangs, the grief of its destruction, the darkness of its encompassment and the unwholesomeness of its taste.

key_terms.دَوَاجِى: Gloom/shades (plural of dawj, referring to covering or enveloping darkness)

ai.seo_question: What are the metaphors for the distress of death in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali employs dense rhetorical imagery, utilizing terms like 'dawaji' (shadows) and 'hanadis' (swamps) to evoke the suffocating and inescapable nature of death's approach, a style characteristic of the eloquent Arabic prose found in Nahj al-Balagha. This passage serves as a spiritual wake-up call, urging believers to cultivate readiness through self-reflection before the sudden onset of the grave's trials. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *mawt* (death) not merely as an end, but as a transitional state requiring continuous spiritual preparation.
